label: Tabs
title: Tabs
summary: Use Tabs to switch between a few peer views of the same content, such as an account’s overview, activity, and details.
corePrinciple: A few peer views, exactly one selected, and the content below follows it.

anatomy.title: A row of tabs, one underlined
anatomy.description: Tabs lines up Tab Items in one row, 16 px apart. The selected tab has a black label and a gold underline; the others are grey.

configuration.title: One row or scrollable
configuration.description: Each tab hugs its label, 16 px from the next, as in Figma. Turn on scrollable when the labels don’t fit, so the row scrolls sideways.
blocks: Three tabs hug their labels from the start of the row.
Each tab hugs its label; scroll the row to reach the rest.

states.title: One tab selected at a time
states.description: The screen keeps track of the selected tab: it marks that tab active and moves the mark when another tab is pressed. Tabs has no disabled or loading state.
blocks: The black label and underline move to the pressed tab.

examples.title: Another tab selected
examples.description: The black label and underline move to the pressed tab.

sizing.title: Hugs its labels, 33 px tall
sizing.description: Tabs stretches to the width of its container. Each tab is 33 px tall: a 17 px label with 8 px above and below, and as wide as its label, with 16 px between tabs. When the tabs don’t fit, every label shrinks and ends in an ellipsis unless the row scrolls.

content.title: Name each view in a word or two
content.description: Labels are short nouns in sentence case that name the view, such as “Overview” or “Activity”. Don’t number tabs or write actions.

inContext.title: Account views over one panel
inContext.description: The screen keeps the selected tab and shows that view below the row. Pressing another tab swaps the panel; the tabs only report the press.

sources.title: Use the public Tabs contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (16 October build) from the team’s private package repository. In Figma and in code, tabs hug their labels with 16 px gaps, and a tab can carry a counter badge. If two tabs are marked active, only the first is selected. The published Storybook predates 0.1.78, so its stories show older labels. On the web the row is a tab list named by its accessibility label, and each tab is announced by its label and whether it is selected. Only the selected tab is in the Tab order, or the first tab when none is selected; Space, Enter, the arrow keys, Home, and End select tabs. In a row that doesn’t scroll, labels that don’t fit end in an ellipsis.
